string.text: The right stick turns in fixed steps. Push it back to the centre before each step.
How far one snap turns you.
The right stick turns continuously. Takes priority over snap turning.
Turning speed at full stick for smooth turning.
Walk with the left stick and turn with the right stick.
Darkens the edges of your view while you move or turn with the sticks, and briefly on each snap turn. 0 turns it off; higher values narrow the view further.

Move with the right stick and turn with the left. The pistol holster, rifle shoulder, ammunition pouch and belt slots are mirrored, the PDA moves to the right side of the chest, and weapons drawn with a key go to the left hand.
Stick travel ignored around the centre. Raise it if you drift while standing still.
How far your real head may move away from the character before it stops. Walls still stop it sooner.
When you step more than 15 cm away from the character in your room, the character walks after you, so walls and enemies meet the body where you are. Off: only your view moves, up to the maximum lean.
How far you can turn your head before your belt, holsters and pockets turn with it. Turning round in your room brings them round; a glance to the side leaves them where they are.
A keyboard key that recenters the view on your character, the same as the vr_recenter console command.
Ducking your real head crouches the character. The right stick crouch still works; the deeper of the two is used.
How far below your standing eye height your head must go to crouch. Your standing height is taken when a level starts or when you recenter.
How far below your standing eye height your head must go for a low crouch.

Squeeze the grip at a place on your belt: binoculars at the buckle, grenade front left, bolt front right, detector behind the ammunition pouch (left), knife behind the pistol holster (right). The PDA hangs on your upper chest (left side) and the inventory is over your left shoulder; four chest pockets below the PDA hold your quick-use items. Carried items hang on the belt.
How close your hand must be to a body slot to use it.
Draw a small ring at a body slot while your hand is within reach of it.
Distance from your eyes down to the belt: holster, ammunition pouch and belt slots. Raise it if they are too high for you.
Sideways distance from your centre to the pistol holster and the ammunition pouch.

Size of PDA message text on the HUD, times its usual size (1 = as on a monitor). Longer messages wrap onto more lines. New messages are laid out at the new size; ones already shown keep their line breaks until they fade.

Meta body tracking bends your arms at your real elbows, moves your shoulders and turns your torso and body places with your real chest. Your hands still follow the controllers. Needs Virtual Desktop's own OpenXR runtime (VDXR) with Forward tracking data to PC on, and Body tracking on in the Quest's Movement tracking settings. A Quest 3 reads your upper body with its cameras; a Quest 2 estimates it from the headset and controllers.
How sure the headset must be of your body before it is used. Raise it if your arms twitch; lower it if body tracking rarely takes over.

Playing seated, reaching down beside your chair toward the real floor brings your hand down to the in-game floor, so you can pick things up. When seated: only when your real floor is well above the game's. Always: whenever it is nearer at all (also for shorter players standing). Your hips, holster and belt are never moved. Needs the Quest boundary (room floor).
Distance between your shoulder joints, about 0.36 m on an average adult. Spreads the shoulder holsters and the chest and pocket places. 0 measures it with body tracking.
From your shoulder joint to your wrist, about 0.60 m on an average adult. Lengthens or shortens the visible arms to yours. 0 measures it with body tracking.
Show your torso and legs, placed from the headset and hands: they follow the game's walking and crouching, and your real crouching and leaning.
Show the pointing rays used to aim at items and usable objects.
Hold weapons the way their first-person animations hold them.
Single shots and hand-worked actions fire as fast as you pull the trigger and work the action, not at the weapon's fire rate. Automatic and burst fire keep it.
Let your hands push loose objects, and also stop against walls and the world.
The weapon in your hands pushes loose objects.
A character you look at shows their name and faction above them within this many metres. 0 never shows it.
Names of items you can pick up show within this many metres of you, measured across the floor. 0 hides them.

Steadies the menu and inventory cursor against controller jitter. Slow, small movements are smoothed; quick sweeps follow the hand almost at once. 0 is off; higher is steadier (10 is about a tenth of a second at rest). Hands and weapons are not affected.
Steadies the hands and the weapon against controller jitter. 0 is off; higher values are steadier but trail the real hand more (10 is about a tenth of a second).

How hard each shot kicks the weapon up and back in your hands, with a pulse in the controller. The kick follows the cartridge and the weight of the weapon, and doubles when a two-handed weapon is held in one hand. 0 turns it off.
Grenades and bolts leave at your hand's speed times this. Raise it if your throws fall short.
Magnified scopes show the game's zoom multiplied by this.
How much larger than the eyepiece glass the scope image is drawn.
Per-eye resolution relative to the headset's recommendation. Higher is sharper and slower. Takes effect after a restart.
Game units per real metre. 1 matches the world to your real size.
Closest distance that is drawn. Lower lets you see hands and sights very close to your eyes.

Draws water in VR with the standard Anomaly water shader (sky reflection only) instead of the Screen Space Shaders water (screen-space reflections, waves, caustics). Much cheaper when a lot of water is in view, and plainer looking. Takes effect immediately.
Render the sun's shadows once for both eyes instead of once per eye. Faster outdoors; turn off to compare.
How far in front of you menus, the PDA and the inventory appear. Closer makes text larger and easier to read; the panel keeps its size.

How far in front of your eyes the in-game HUD (ammunition count, PDA messages, hints) floats. Closer makes it look larger, as a sheet of paper brought nearer, and its corner elements move further out from the centre with it. Separate from the menu distance.

How large the in-game HUD is at its distance. Higher makes the ammunition count and messages larger but moves them further toward the edges of your view; lower pulls them in toward the centre, where the lenses are sharpest, and makes them smaller. Size and distance together set how much of your view the HUD covers (Size 1 at 1 m: about 75 degrees across).

Gives the headset runtime each eye's depth, so frames it has to reproject (when the game misses the headset's frame rate) can keep near objects steady. Off by default: it costs GPU time every frame, and Virtual Desktop showed no visible gain from it. Turn it on only if your runtime uses depth and near objects swim when it reprojects.
Detail of the magnified scope image: pixels rendered per pixel the lens covers in your eye. 1 matches the headset; higher is sharper and slower. 0 renders it at full eye resolution, as before.

Look at the back of your off-hand wrist, forearm across your view as when reading a watch: bars show health (red) and stamina (yellow), plus radiation (green), psy health (blue), bleeding (dark red) and hunger (brown) when they matter.
Hide the game's flat on-screen status indicators in VR (use the wrist display instead). Messages and script HUD elements still show.
Seated uses the headset's local space; standing uses the room-scale stage when the runtime offers one.
Desktop, VR when a headset is available (automatic), or always try VR. The -vr and -novr launch options override this. Takes effect after a restart.
Draw controller axes and write pose, input and timing details to the log.
Sprayed droplets, stains where they land, and blood that stays on walls and floors. Off restores the original blood marks and hit effects. DX11 renderer without MSAA only.
Droplet count, stain detail and how much stained surface stays in video memory (about 8, 45, 90 or 180 MB). Changing it keeps existing stains.
Fresh blood spreads into pools on floors and runs down walls for a few seconds. Not available at Low quality.
Wounds bleed down the clothing as a growing run, drawn by the body's own shader, instead of small blood marks. Experimental. Needs the blood shader mod.
How much blood a wound releases: the number of jets and how much each leaves on walls and floors. 1 is the default.
How wide and how fast blood sprays from a wound. Lower keeps it in tight jets close to the body; higher throws it further and wider.
Droplets drawn along each jet. Higher looks more solid and costs a little more GPU time.
Stains farther away are not drawn. They are kept and come back when you return.
Flying droplets farther away are not drawn.
How long fresh blood takes to darken and lose its wet shine.
When blood takes longer than this on the GPU, droplet counts and distances are reduced until it fits again. 0 turns this off.
Write blood CPU and GPU times, droplet and page counts to the console every two seconds.
